ingredients.item: /2 head green or red leaf lettuce , torn into bite pieces, washed and spun bone-dry
A splash of rice vinegar , optional

instructions.heading: Step 1
instructions.action: The dressing stirred together in the serving bowl — gochugaru, soy, honey, garlic — into a loose paste.
instructions.visualOrTactileCue: tastes a shade too strong on a fingertip; the lettuce's water will round it, same law as every fresh bowl in this family.

instructions.heading: Step 2
instructions.action: Lettuce in, tossed with two spoons or hands — #B04's massage minute — until every leaf wears the red-flecked gloss. Sesame oil, seeds, scallion over.
instructions.visualOrTactileCue: the leaf test: crisp, cold, dressed-through — spicy-savory on the first bite, the leaf's clean sweetness after, no dressing pooling at the bowl's floor. Serve beside any of the M-list's records; it is the freshest possible counter to the gochujang lanes (#M04, #M13).

visualDonenessCues: tastes a shade too strong on a fingertip; the lettuce's water will round it, same law as every fresh bowl in this family.

the leaf test: crisp, cold, dressed-through — spicy-savory on the first bite, the leaf's clean sweetness after, no dressing pooling at the bowl's floor. Serve beside any of the M-list's records; it is the freshest possible counter to the gochujang lanes (#M04, #M13).
storageNotes: Undressed lettuce keeps 2 days in paper towel; the dressed bowl does not keep — by design.
Variations: cucumber pieces folded in; the cabbage version (#B04) for a sturdier bowl; a drop of cho-gochujang (#SA03) thinned as the dressing for the sweet-heat fork.
